item.title: Tottori Sand Dunes: Japan's Great Coastal Desert — Guide
item.description: The Tottori Sand Dunes are the largest and best-known sand dunes in Japan, a great sweep of wind-sculpted sand running some 16 kilometres along the Sea of Japan coast and reaching up to 50 metres high. Formed over a hundred thousand years by sand carried down from the mountains and shaped by the wind, they present a genuinely desert-like landscape, complete with rippled ridges, a large basin and a tall dune, the ‘horse’s back’, from which visitors look out over the deep blue sea.
